/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/:
COMMENT: All comments by JCH are denoted (JCH).
         "I actually started making music on the Amiga, in the note-based
         program Aegis Sonix. I then wrote my first C64 player in 1987
         (I was 21) and converted the notes by meticulously writing it down
         on paper first. Although SoundMonitor had arrived at that point, I
         didn't like it much and thus never considered using it." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/2cVee.sid:
COMMENT: "Experimental tune with music in 2 voices and 9 sfx in the third
         voice. This was the first time I ever did this." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/42nd_Street.sid:
COMMENT: "A very weird tune with a very weird ending. After I named the tune
         '42nd Street' I played it in a driver on the C64 which could display
         the time - and to my surprise it lasted exactly 42 seconds." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Accident.sid:
COMMENT: "Cooperation between Morten Sigaard Kristensen and I. The bass was
         taken from a pophit and I made the rest on top of it." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Acid_1988.sid: COMMENT: "Made in 1988 but packed and released several years later." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Ages.sid:
COMMENT: "This was one of the first tunes I entirely made on the keyboard
         before bonging it into the editor. Normally, most music was composed
         directly on the computer without the aid of a synthesizer keyboard."
         (JCH)

TITLE: Trapped
 ARTIST: Jens-Christian Huus (JCH)
COMMENT: "The name refers to the ring modulation effect which sounds like a car
         screeching to its doom." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Cause_I_Love_Her_So.sid:
COMMENT: "A worktune where I imagined the words above 'sung' to the notes from
         14-30 seconds of play. The part from 00:30 was later extracted to form
         the release song 'Real_Shit.sid'." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Caveman.sid: COMMENT: "Another cooperation between Morten Sigaard Kristensen and I." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Chordian.sid:
COMMENT: "This tune was sent to a guy in England who promised to use it in a
         game with credits by Vibrants. However, it seems as if he liked it so
         much that he put his very own credits on the game..." (JCH)
         The game is named Stack Up (1991 by Zeppelin Games) and the guy is
         Gerard 'Gez' Gourley/Sonic Graffiti.
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Coops_Ups.sid:
COMMENT: "Here Morten Sigaard Kristensen managed to make most of the tune and
         then 'invited' me to do the solo in the end of it." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Cotune_2.sid:
COMMENT: "A cooperation tune 'DRAX' and I tried to do. He did the bass, drums
         and chords and I tried to do the leader. I soon ran out of inspiration
         and the tune was never finished." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Crowdnoise.sid:
COMMENT: "The last sound I ever did on the C64, made July 1992. At that time I
         had been away from the C64 for months, playing around with the PC -
         however, a guy in 'Pretzel Logic' said he needed a crowdnoise effect,
         so I did it. The demo he worked on was AFAIK never released." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Darkness_IV.sid:
COMMENT: "The last song I did in the old player system. Also the only one not
         composed in Aegis Sonix, it was done in Sound Tracker on Amiga - yes,
         one of the first versions from Karsten Obarski. It was still converted
         using the old awkward system though." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Demogame_Example.sid:
COMMENT: "This block was made as the first of seven planned leveltunes. It was
         ordered by a guy in 'Bonzai', shortly after I met 'Trap' of 'Bonzai'
         for the first time. This was the second attempt after the 'Golddigger'
         project. The game was never finished." (JCH)

COMMENT: "Made at Jewels' place. I tried to emulate the style of Diflex as

         This tune was used in a game titled "Soccer 7".
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Dont_Be_Sad.sid:
COMMENT: "The first 30 seconds was 'inspired' by an Amiga song I found in a new
         tracker on that computer." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Double_Speed.sid:
COMMENT: "This is the only quickspeed tune not made in v17.Q0. It was made in
         1989, some time before Jeroen Tel made his first quatro-tune for
         'Invest'. However, the idea was not new at that time. In the
         mid-eighties Tony Crowther experimented with quatro players in games
         such as 'Zig Zag'. My double speed tune, however, used the ordinary v9
         player and was simply called twice a frame." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Easy_Does_It.sid:
COMMENT: "Notice how I put real synthesizer chords into the digi voice. That
         was not done very often on the Commodore 64 - musicians normally used
         this channel for bass and drums only. The tune makes extensive use of
         ring modulation effects and was used in a 'Pretzel Logic' demo." (JCH)

 ARTIST: Morten Hansen (ICE)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Farting.sid:
COMMENT: "Thrown together in a few minutes to show a friend how to use the
         editor." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Feel_It.sid:
COMMENT: "Another tune that was packed and released at a much later date."
         (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Fiasko_2.sid:
COMMENT: "This was in fact the first suggestion to the 'Oswald' game. I played
         the tune to the programmer and graphician of the game but they didn't
         like it. They loved the next attempt however, which you can find as
         'Super_Oswald.sid'." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Five_Minutes.sid: COMMENT: "As the name suggests it was done in a hurry on Aegis Sonix." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Fooled.sid:
COMMENT: "Introtune made in an experimental player called 'Intro Player'. The
         player took very little rastertime but suffered under too many
         compromises. I only made this tune in the player." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/George_Carl.sid:
COMMENT: "A long tune containing three completely different parts. The slow
         introduction changes at 01:19 to a part which was played by the clown
         George Carl during his shows. Here I tried to emulate a real mouth
         organ using ring modulation." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Glider_Pilot.sid:
TITLE: Glider Pilot
 ARTIST: <?>
COMMENT: "This was a conversion from an old C64 game of the same name. The
         composition was very nice but used horribly raw sounds. I converted
         the tune and it was used in the demo that won the C64 demo competition
         at the Randers copy-party. The original is in the HVSC as
         /GAMES/G-L/Glider_Pilot.sid" (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Golddigger.sid:
COMMENT: "This was the first real game-music project I did. It was planned as a
         cooperation between Link and I after meeting each other for the first
         time in february 1989. The music itself was supposed to have been used
         for a 'Boulder Dash' clone, but the Danish software house 'The New
         Electronic Generation' did not survive its first game." (JCH)

/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Gunfight.sid:
COMMENT: "I managed to code a complete Gunfight game in 1987-1988 - you know,
         the stuff with two gunfighters in each side of the screen shooting
         each other until one of them enters 'BOOT HILL'. This tune was made in
         'Aegis Sonix' - the only tune to be converted using the old method
         into Laxity's player." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Hacktrick.sid:
COMMENT: "My friend, 'The Saint', hummed the bassline and I made all the rest."
         (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Hard_On.sid:
COMMENT: "The first song done in a player featuring 'Hard restart' - so as you
         see, the name is not as naughty as you might think! ;)" (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Hawaii.sid:
COMMENT: "A very long tune containing one of the longest solo parts I have ever
         done in a C64 tune. The bassline and drums were originally made by
         Morten Sigaard Kristensen, but in the end I 'raped' it so much that it
         virtually became my own work. The solo part starts at 01:39. Notice
         how the tune decays in the end - this was very unusual on the C64."
         (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Heavy_Hit.sid:
COMMENT: "Short, 'end-of-level-monster'-like tune made in a compromise player
         which took VERY little rastertime." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Hexagon_Party.sid:
COMMENT: "Made FOR that party, not AT it. The tune contains quite a lot of
         harmonic mistakes, something I often made in that period. These were
         often caused by 'lazy' transpositions of the bassline sequence -
         instead of creating a new one." (JCH)

/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Hurricane.sid:

         managed to get a version of this sourcecode - and tried to fiddle with

         changes after 15 seconds." (JCH)

COMMENT: "Conversion of a 007 theme found on a CD containing James Bond
         synthesizer conversions." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Jewels.sid:
TITLE: Wouldn't It Be Good [from Human Racing]
 ARTIST: Nik Kershaw
COMMENT: "Conversion of an old Nik Kershaw song. The first version of the old
         player to feature slide. Many of the tunes in this period didn't use
         any slide at all." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Kinetic.sid:
TITLE: Kinetic [from the Amiga MOD module]
 ARTIST: Stefan Jaworski (Nightlight)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Knackdick.sid:
COMMENT: "The only real cooperation tune released by DRAX and I. I must admit
         however, that DRAX made about 85% of the tune." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/L_L_L.sid:
COMMENT: "The first tune made in Laxity's. Not 100% my own composition since I
         left parts of the instruments and bassline intact (try to compare it
         with /MUSICIANS/L/Laxity/Ikari_Intro_Song.sid)." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Labyrint.sid:
TITLE: Labyrinth [from the Amiga game]
 ARTIST: N.J. Luuring Jr.
COMMENT: "A television quiz program which was made popular by a great Danish
         former disc-jockey Kim Schumacher was converted by a small Danish firm
         as a C64 game. The music was composed on the Amiga by an unknown guy.
         'DRAX' was asked to convert the tune for a certain sum of money but,
         as he said himself, he wasn't sure he could convert it so he asked me
         for help. I completed the conversion for the ridiculous sum of money.
         Later, 'DRAX' admitted that he didn't complete the conversion because
         he thought the original Amiga music was boring. I must confess that he
         has a point there." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Lady_Lisa.sid:
COMMENT: "This tune was composed and then put on ice, only to be packed and
         released at a much later date." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Last_One.sid:
COMMENT: "The last tune I made in Laxity's player until Laxity told me to stop
         using his player. I then began coding a new player system and later an
         editor as well." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Little_Test.sid:
COMMENT: "The second tune I did after 'Better late than never'. Most samples
         were sampled from the Korg M1 using Commodore's own hardware sampler
         which plugged into the cartridge port. It makes VERY extensive use of
         ring modulation and hard sync." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Lonewolf.sid:
COMMENT: "The only tune made in the compromise player v07. The player was too
         awkward to use any further." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Mad4.sid:
COMMENT: "Maduplec of 'BUDS', a very prominent coder in the demo scene became
         quite an alrounder in the later C64 days. Making close to everything
         himself he painted the graphics, coded, composed and even made a music
         editor with his own player. He sent me a version of it to me for
         testing, and this is the result. The player takes very little
         rastertime. I remember that when I sent him the tune he told me it was
         'typically me'." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Maduplec3.sid:
COMMENT: "It is a slow tune - today, I actually think it sounds best if you
         play it a THREE times the speed in SidPlay instead of the usual TWO.
         It has nothing to do with 'Maduplec' from 'Buds' other than the name
         itself." (JCH)
(#1)
COMMENT: This tune is played at the original 2x speed.
(#2)
COMMENT: This tune is the same as tune #1, but is played at 3x speed.
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Maniac_Mansion.sid:
TITLE: Maniac Mansion, Tune #1 [from the game]
 ARTIST: Chris Grigg & David Lawrence
COMMENT: "I was impressed with the titletune on 'Maniac Mansion', an adventure
         game by LucasFilm (that was years before they changed their name to
         LucasArts). However, the instruments were rubbish so I did my very own
         version of it. At a silent part in the end of the tune I even added a
         few notes of my own." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Maniaxion.sid: COMMENT: Later used in the titlescreen of the game Pitfighter, (C) 1991 Domark.
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Martin_4.sid:
COMMENT: "Apart from using the drumset from the 'Batman'-tune, I experimented
         with the pulse Martin Galway made in the 'Rambo' highscore tune."
         (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Mayday_v3.sid:
TITLE: Stranded in Iowa
 ARTIST: Manfred Mann
COMMENT: "Parts of the song was actually inspired by an old Manfred Mann song
         called 'Stranded in Iowa'." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Memory_I.sid:
COMMENT: "Even though it was composed in the same month as where the editor was
         finished, it was put on ice only to be properly packed and released
         some years later." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Michelle.sid:
COMMENT: "Another two-in-one tune, one of the better of that period. Especially
         the last part is IMHO still nice." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Misjudge.sid:
COMMENT: "The second of the three tunes I did in the compromise player v19
         which takes very little rastertime." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Modemtrading.sid:
COMMENT: "A silly little song I did in my modem trading days. If you listen
         carefully you can hear a telephone ringing - followed by a modem
         connecting." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Moonlight.sid:
COMMENT: "This is the very first song I ever composed. It happened on Aegis
         Sonix on the Amiga. I remember I was very proud - today, I wonder
         why..." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Multivoice_2.sid:
COMMENT: "Here I experimented with the idea of using arpeggio to simulate a lot
         of voices. It didn't turn out too great, though." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Need_You_Tonight_v1.sid:
TITLE: Need You Tonight [from Kick]
 ARTIST: INXS
COMMENT: "Conversion of the old Inxs hit. Later in 1989 I made another attempt
         because the demogroup Jewels wanted a better conversion." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Need_You_Tonight_v2.sid:
TITLE: Need You Tonight [from Kick]
 ARTIST: INXS
COMMENT: "The second conversion I did of this tune, ordered by 'Excell' from

         sequencepacker. I put a lot of work into making the conversion

/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/No_Birthday.sid:
COMMENT: "Shorter version of 'Birthday' without the silly birthday song in the
         beginning." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Ode_to_JO.sid:
COMMENT: "Made after I heard one of JO's terrific 'hard restart' songs. I was
         impressed with the way his ADSR worked on his chord sounds, so I tried
         to do the same thing. However, I didn't really know what it was until
         JO told me how it was done. I then implemented it from player v11."
         (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Ode_to_the_64.sid:
COMMENT: "I tried to make a tune like Rob Hubbard's 'One Man and his Droid',

         for 'Pit Fighter'. It was probably in 1991 - I remember I made an

/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Playertest.sid:

/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Push-It.sid:
COMMENT: "The Danish demogroup 'Jewels' also fiddled with a puzzle game, called
         'Push-It'. This is the intro tune, one of my favourite tunes from the
         C64 period. It uses a double voice drum and was heavily inspired by
         the music from 'Task III'. The game itself was never finished. You may
         have to fiddle with filter parameters to make that snare drum sound
         the way it should." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Push-It_main.sid:

/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Rain_Funk.sid:
COMMENT: "Released in a demo at the Randers copy-party, IMHO the very best C64

/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Real_Good.sid:
COMMENT: "Named so because I liked the result when I made it in 1988/1989. I
         remember I was so disappointed when I learned that 'Einstein' of
         'Upfront' didn't like it." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Real_Shit.sid:
COMMENT: "Actually extracted from a worktune called 'Cause I Love Her So'. I
         liked the start of the worktune but I thought this part didn't really
         belong so I extracted it to form a separate song and made a lot of
         fast solo's on top of it." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Revenge.sid:
COMMENT: "Here I deliberately tried to put together a lot of chords in a song
         which shifts in and out of the minor and major scales." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Revolutionary.sid:
COMMENT: "This was the first tune done in the final editor, hence the name."
         (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Sampler_1.sid:
COMMENT: Contains four tunes. One of the tunes was extracted to form the single
         tune "Hoppin'".

/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Secret_Land.sid:

 ARTIST: Sandra Cretu
COMMENT: "Conversion of a hitsong from Sandra. I put a lot of work into making
         the conversion accurate. Made just before the party in Slagelse."
         (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Shadow_Sun.sid:
COMMENT: "This was one of the last tunes I composed in an assembler listing. My
         editor was almost complete and after trying it, I never wanted to
         compose music in assembler again." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Sharks_game.sid:
COMMENT: "The only real gametrack in the old player, containing 4 tunes. It was

COMMENT: "A tune where I tried to emulate the style of Maniacs of Noise. As the
         title suggests, parts of the notes matches the words so you can
         actually sing the title to it. Try it after 9-12 seconds of play! :)"
         (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Shift.sid:
COMMENT: "A worktune that wasn't finished. Due to the fact that we have reached
         1991, my Korg M1 was a reality. This tune was totally composed on the
         keyboard first, apart from the digi voice which was added later using
         the editor alone. The digi voice doesn't appear until 01:16 - it was
         supposed to be a 'surprise' tune. This was also the last digital tune
         I did - and as far as I can remember, the very last C64 tune as well."
         (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Short_n_Sad.sid:
COMMENT: "Made in player v01 - the player now contained an arpeggio table
         routine for the drums." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Shorty.sid:
COMMENT: "Very short introtune made for a Dominators intro I coded myself."
         (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Simple_Tune.sid:
COMMENT: "This was the first tune I did in my own player after leaving Laxity's
         player. There are absolutely no effects other than pure notes in this
         song." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Skaermtrolden_Hugo.sid:
TITLE: Hugo Rap [from Hugo Rap!]
 ARTIST: George Keller (Skaermtrolden Hugo)
COMMENT: "A professional software house in Denmark called 'SilverRock' gained a
         lot of success with 'Hugo' in danish television. This troll could be
         controlled in a game using telephone buttons. A very new concept which
         soon became enormously popular. During the success of the troll, a
         real musician produced a CD containing a rap hit where Hugo was
         singing using the typical voice which was also used in the game. As
         the game was converted for sales versions from the Amiga to PC and
         C64, I did the C64 song converted from the Danish rap hit." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Slapbass.sid:
COMMENT: "A long tune based on a slapbass. The result doesn't really sound like
         a slapbass, but I couldn't get any closer at the time. Some years
         later, a Dutch guy proved that by using the $51 waveform, you COULD
         get quite close indeed!" (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Song_Made_in_Monitor.si:
COMMENT: "The only tune I ever did in a machinecode monitor. I knew that Laxity
         made all his music this way and I wanted to try it out. Although I
         managed to compose a tune, I didn't like the method at all." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Spaceport.sid:
TITLE: Spaceport [from the Amiga game]
 ARTIST: Holger Gehrmann
COMMENT: "Conversion from the titletune of an old 'reLINE' game on the Amiga -
         one of my friends asked me if I would convert it." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Strike_Force.sid:
TITLE: Strike Force Introtune
 ARTIST: Markus Schneider
COMMENT: "Conversion of the old Strike Force introtune - originally composed by
         'Diflex'. I tried to be fair to the atmosphere of the original
         introtune." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Su-Sweet.sid:
COMMENT: "Speaking of puzzle games, the German software house 'Double Density'
         was a master at releasing such games. One of them was the game
         'Su-Sweet'. I was contacted and asked to do the soundtrack within a
         very tight deadline. This is the music for the game - it was done in
         march 1991." (JCH)

/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Tecnetium.sid:
COMMENT: "I always get mixed feelings when I play this music. The title- tune
         is long and I put a lot of work into it in april 1989, but today I can
         hear loads of harmonic errors here and there. The game was done for a
         sideways shoot'em up which a couple of totally unknown danish guys was
         making. They soon lost all interest in their game, however. The
         hiscore theme was a conversion of the old Cliff Richard hit
         'Congratulations' done right out my head. I always wanted to make such
         a hiscore tune, because I always thought Rob Hubbard did it all wrong
         when he made 'sad' hiscore tunes. It is a sad thing when the game
         ends, but getting a high score is supposed to be a GOOD thing! :)"
         (JCH)

/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Test_04_3.sid:
COMMENT: "The last tune I did in player v04 for the sequence-less editor. This

         chords on a keyboard, something that was very unusual in this period."

/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Test_10_2.sid: COMMENT: "This was later packed and spread as 'Memory I'." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Test_11_1.sid: COMMENT: "Finetune test where two of the voices are phased together." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Test_12_2_harmonic_hell: COMMENT: "Last tune in the 'Test'-series. I tried to make it title-like." (JCH)

/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Test_in_Zoolooks_Player:
COMMENT: "A small test tune I made while helping my group mate Zoolook improve
         his own player." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Training.sid: COMMENT: "One of the first songs where I used a double voice drum." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Trapped.sid:
COMMENT: "This tune was originally made for a demo by 'Trap' of 'Bonzai'. The
         melodic change at 02:55 was later extracted to form its own tune
         called 'Carcrash'." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Triangle_1.sid:
COMMENT: "Attempt at making the SID chip say 'Triangle' using ring modulation
         in three voices. Judge by yourself if you think I succeded! ;) There
         are three attempts in all." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Tuned_In.sid:
COMMENT: "The first player v01 with a few decent effects. If you listen closely

         my hands off his player. The Future Composer was a hack editor on

         note but not during the note. As to whether I managed to match his

/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Wizax_Demo.sid:

         unlocks the noise in such a way that the noise waveform sounds more
         metallic. However, I later discovered that this worked differently
         from C64 to C64. On some C64, I had to lock the waveform with $F0,
         where other versions required $F8 to achieve the same effect." (JCH)
/MUSICIANS/J/JCH/X-Ray.sid:

/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/63_speed_music:
COMMENT: "Ray kept saying "Make more mutispeed music", so I did. Actully, it
         only runs channel #1 at 63x, the other two channels run at 9x, but oh
         well :). And it's too short... I very quickly got annoyed with the
         unresponsiveness of the editor when trying to play sounds at this
         rate. But I *do* like working with the sounds at these sort of update
         rates, so I'm working on a player which takes a smaller amount of
         raster time than TFX to use for such music. (That said, one of PCH's
         TFX songs (supposedly) runs a channel at 72x, but that's just too
         insane to dicuss :)." (JJ)
/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Archnial.sid:
COMMENT: "The title of this song comes from my friend Jenn's AIM screenname,
         whom I love dearly (in a completly plutonic way, for the record).
         She doesn't understand the 'c64 thing'. I always wanted to be able to
         write funk tunes like Drax, and later Mitch&Dane, do, and despite it
         coming almost dead last in the c64.sk SID competition, I think I
         succeeded somewhat. I actually like a lot of the harmonic work in
         this song, as did my sister, who yelled at me after she first heard it
         for being able to pull it off! Of course, most people disagreed with
         her accusation of me pulling it off." (JJ)
/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Archnial_Trian:
COMMENT: "Someone on c64.sk made the statement that to do well, you need to
         make songs which only use the triangle wave. So I did, and I think it
         sounds a lot like something you'd hear on a NES. I actually prefer
         this version myself." (JJ)
/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Blood_Starligh:
NAME: Blood, Starlight, Rain Like Tears.
COMMENT: "Sitting in a backpackers hostel in sydney, get a call from my
         parents, I can't come home, they've rented out my room. I've been here
         for 5 weeks now, but only finally got a laptop this day. I was feeling
         incredibly dark, having spent the last week in bed ill, I really
         wanted to go home, or failing that, I wanted someone to take a few
         minutes out of their day to see if I was still alive (okay, so I was
         feeling kind of melodramatic, lol), This girl promised to hang out
         with me, and then cancelled or forgot every time for weeks straight,
         and I was stupid (read: thinking with my heart instead of my head)
         and didn't want to acknowlage that she was ignoring me... I was
         losing my mind, and this music represents that.
         The full verse is "Blood, Starlight, Rain like tears, Drink from
         this, and let go the years". I don't know who penned those words, but
         I dropped the latter half from the title because I promised said girl
         that I would.
         This music was made on an emulator (vice 1.8, and of course I had
         resid turned on :-p). It was also one of my bigger expermients with
         filters synced from different channels to the one they're targetting.
         If it works at all on a real C64, I'd consider myself very lucky, lol,
         because I didn't have access to one at the time." (JJ)
/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Chase_That_Fee:
TITLE: The Most Beautiful Girl in the World [from The Gold Experience]
 ARTIST: Prince
/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Colors.sid:
COMMENT: "I sat down to create an ending music for the WOW demo 'Evolution',
         with this text that I'd just written in my mind, and eight hours
         later, I had most of this. It isn't (deliberatly) covering anything,
         the resemblence to some other music is just a coincidence :).
         Ironically, this is one of my happiest musics, and yet at the time I
         made it, I was depressed and suicidal. Life is full of contrasts, I
         guess that's what makes it special.
         Well, that and Ray finally fixing the restart bug in TFX :-p." (JJ)
/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Drymouth.sid:

TITLE: Title [from the Game Boy Color game Drymouth]
 ARTIST: Jakob Kaufman (virt)
COMMENT: "See the entry for Drymouth. I couldn't decided between these two

/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Eternal_Repris:

COMMENT: "This was inspired by a song named "Eternal" by Evanescence. It was
         originally going to be a cover of said song, however that went awry
         within the first 10 seconds or so :). The second half is mostly an
         experiment in what happens when you mix diffrent types of Ringmod and
         Sync effects, which I like the sound of. Sidplay1 hates it. It was
         originally intended to sound quite different from this, because the
         original sketch for it required a dyanmic wave table, but I got fed up
         waiting for that, and finished it as is." (JJ)
/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Evolution.sid:
COMMENT: "I try, I fly, I lie, I cry, I die. My mis-understood epic. Everyone
         except for Ray hated this :). It started out as soundmon clone music
         (intended for the WOW demo of the same name), an evolution in music,
         you know, the idea being that I've also got future composer type music
         (see TFX == future composer), and the other guys were going to do
         modern music blah blah watever, I forget the details. Anyhow, around
         2 minutes after I sat down at the editor, it instead became something
         else (I hate it when that happens :-p), which basically amounts to an
         attempt to place what was goes through my mind at the time into SID
         form... the evolution of my soul. I achieved that, I think, which is
         probably why almost no-one else understands it. I personally like
         this music better than any other which I have ever made, however my
         emotional attachment to it makes me biased." (JJ)
/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Exuding_Titlen:
TITLE: Exuding Titleness [from the Scream Tracker 3 module]
 ARTIST: Andrew Sega (Necros)
COMMENT: "PG Gave me a copy of this on a CD when I was in the Czech Republic
         during 2000, and I instantly fell in love with it, and as soon as I
         arrived home to my C64, this cover of it was the first thing I did.
         It was done in kind of a hurry, as I had other things on my mind, and
         so it could be significantly better than it is, but it's still not
         terrible, overall." (JJ)
/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Fields_of_Inno:
TITLE: Fields of Innocence [from Origin]
 ARTIST: Evanescence
COMMENT: "Only a partial cover... initially I set out to do a full cover of
         this, however in the end I only covered the the lead and background

         Kind of a waste, really, because the original is much better than I

         6581 filter in places... on an 8580, some things just don't sound
         quite right :(.
         Anthony Bisset, from Digiradi/DSP Audio remixed this and layed vocals
         over it." (JJ)

         width modulation on the bass notes, which makes the drums sound
         harder. Anyhow, I stopped using that editor/player, because I found
         it far too limiting." (JJ)

TITLE: The Follower [from the Impulse Tracker module]
 ARTIST: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)
COMMENT: "See the comment for v1. This version has pulse width modulation on

/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Forever.sid:
COMMENT: "This was inspired by the music from the PC demo 'Forever' by Acme. I
         don't recall who did that music, but this doesn't actully sound much
         at all like it... but you should listen to that music if you can find
         it, because it's really good. There is another story that goes with
         this music, which explains the in binary message, which starts, as
         all good stories does, 'Well, there was this girl...' :). Her name
         was Sonja, and she didn't.
         But she was leaning over my shoulder when I was packing this tune, and
         is the only girlfriend I've had who has even tollerated, let alone
         understood, my C64 obsession. As a birthday surprise for me, she made
         a C64 music. It was surprisingly good for a first ever SID piece!
         One day, it may see the light of day, but today is not that day." (JJ)
/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Game_Over_view:
COMMENT: "This was the music from the first ever Game Over(view), and was
         written for it the day before it was released (at the start of 2004).
         It was an attempt to do a song in the same style as Detert's Game On
         11/93, and although it didn't quite turn out that way, I like how it
         ended up." (JJ)
/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Green_Hill.sid:
TITLE: You Can Do Anything (Toot Toot Sonic Warr.) [from the GG game Sonic 2]
 ARTIST: Masafumi Ogata
COMMENT: "I beat this game in a couple of hours when it first came out, but
         always loved the music, and this tune in particular. Fast forward to
         mid 2000, and I'm sitting in a backpackers hostel in Prague with my
         gamegear, and I have no alarm clock and a 9am flight to catch, with my
         girlfriend (who I hadn't seen for 5 months) is waiting on the other
         end of it. So hence I can't really go to sleep (I'd die if I missed
         said flight :-p), but hey, I have a gamegear with this game, and so I
         play until Green Hill zone, and then listen to this music for 7 hours
         straight, at which point I finally ran out of spare lives and
         continues.
         Fast forward to June/July 2001, and I've got some weird illness where
         I can't stand up or hold down food (never did work out what the was,
         heh), and my girlfriend runs away to america because the idea that
         for once in her life she has to be an adult is to damned hard to deal
         with (Hey, Gundam Wing Hentai is much more fun), and I havn't slept
         for 2 weeks or eaten in 4 weeks (not an exaggeration), which has had
         the predictable effects on my mind. Crawl over to my C64, load TFX,
         bury myself of memories of that night in Prague and happy fun music!
         Only digital love is eternal." (JJ)
/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Green_Hill_Rep:
TITLE: You Can Do Anything (Toot Toot Sonic Warr.) [from the GG game Sonic 2]
 ARTIST: Masafumi Ogata
/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Happy_Happy_Jo:
COMMENT: "Despite my first C64 music being made in 1988, this is probably the
         first one I did which wasn't complete and utter crap (Well, maybe this
         and "Not so JCH based", but it was done on a bad emulator and breaks
         on a real C64, it turns out ^_^. Maybe one day I'll remake it and
         release it, because the ideas in it were good, just bad implentation
         as is the usual thing with me :). It wasn't until later that year
         the the message penetrated my brain that, if you want to make an
         okay music, you need to spend more than an hour on it ;). If I was
         running WOW, I would have kicked me out for being completly lame ;).
         But hey, I learned my lesson (sort of....)" (JJ)

 ARTIST: Alberto Jose Gonzalez
COMMENT: "This is loosely based on something that I heard once on a NES. What,

/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Internalise.si:
COMMENT: "This was inspired by what I remembered of Ash Hogg's Spellcast title
         music, however it turns out that even the part I thought I'd stolen
         (the background lead that plays at the start) bears not much
         resemblence to it. Go figure. This is another music, like evolution,
         which is really a reflection of my psyche at the time, however this
         one didn't get the negative reaction which evolution did :). People
         did tell me that it's too short, however, and they're right. But cest
         la vie.
         A shame that I couldn't make a really big and fearsome snare,
         though..." (JJ)

 ARTIST: Charles Deenen

/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Midi_Drums.sid:
TITLE: Midi Drums [from the midi module]
 ARTIST: Jaymz Julian
COMMENT: "This is the second attempt I made to do this song on the C64, and was
         in fact the song that TFX table variables were created for. I
         originally tried to do this in Sid Duzz It in early 1999, but the
         number of arpeggio commands required for the places where there is
         two leads in one channel, and the blips in the drum/bass channel,
         overwelmed that editor. So I tried in JCH v20g4, where I had managed
         to succed with Sunset Spirals, due to the ability it has to change the
         wavetable from within a song, but this too was not to be, due to the
         limitations of the editor. So, I started writing a new editor, which
         was specifically designed to handle this situation, by splitting each
         channel into six virtual channels, and using special rules to modulate
         them together. But this took up a lot of ram and raster time, indeed
         it too so much ram in the editor that I could only store five patterns
         at a time, so this was not to be either. So Ray introduced me to TFX,
         and I asked him about changing the wave table from within the song,
         but he wouldn't have this, because it would confuse people, but he
         suggested a viable alternative, which is to support variables in the
         wave table, and promised to add this feature asap. That was January
         2001, but he was too busy to implement them for the next two and a
         half years. So I started bugging him to just give me the source and
         the bits to build it, and in November 2003, he did. So, I put my
         money where my mouth was, and added that feature (and a bunch of
         others which I had been wanting for a long time), and I was _finally_
         able to do a version of this that I happy with. To anyone else but
         me, this is just another mediocre game tune, but for me it was an
         achievement." (JJ)
/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Pacmania.sid:
TITLE: Block Town [from the arcade game Pac-Mania]
 ARTIST: Yoshito Tomuro
COMMENT: "Anyone who played the arcade game much knows that Ben's cover of it
         was a bit crap (I'd blame a lack of channels on the C64 for harmonies,
         but his amiga version is just as crap), and everyone else's C64 covers
         seem to cover his crap version, not the arcade version. So, my
         version is crap too, but I think it has the nice harmonies in the
         second half, at least, and I think is a little less crap than his :)."
         (JJ)
/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Pentagonal_Dre:
TITLE: Pentagonal Dreams [from the ScreamTracker S3M module]
 ARTIST: Andrew Sega (Necros)
/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Purple_Sky.sid:
TITLE: Purple Sky II [from the Scream Tracker 3 module]
 ARTIST: Jonne Valtonen (Purple Motion)
COMMENT: "After Sunset Sprirals, I was once again fed up with JCH's editor, and
         wanted something better. Ray had suggested to me using TFX several
         times before, and I finally got some documentation for it, and so now
         was the time to use it. I had the S3M of this kicking around, and so
         I covered it to learn the editor. The instruments suck... I never was
         good at making percussion, and unfortunantly there isn't any good ones
         around made in TFX to rip. I also had basically zero understanding of
         how the wave tables worked when I did this, and as a result there are
         some very stupid things in there which sound terrible ;). This
         probably should never have been released, but people liked it for
         reasons that I don't understand.
         As it turned out, the instruments sounded so crap partially because
         Ray's player was horrifically bugged, at the time. I recompiled it
         against a later player, and it sounds a LOT better." (JJ)
/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Rasterman.sid:
TITLE: Flop Magazine 41 [from the Atari XL/XE music]
 ARTIST: Radek Sterba (Raster)
COMMENT: "So, TFX 2.9 still wasn't here, but I wanted to cover this 4 channel
         music from the atari, so what I did, is set the player to 1 frame per
         row, and then enter all of the arpeggios by hand. I'm surprised it
         didn't make the file much larger than it is. It was a pain in the
         ass, but I'm quite pleased with the result." (JJ)
/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Rekonstruct.si:
COMMENT: "This song is made up entirely of patterns from Fishmagic, but played
         a different tempo's and in a differnet order. It was originally
         intended to be used in a demo with fishmagic, so I was going for that
         similar but different effect, and I think it worked very well. But,
         ironically, I was never happy enough with the original fishmagic, or
         how the demo was turning out, so I gave this to Jazzcat for an issue
         of Vandalism News, for which it was much more suitable anyhow. I love
         this sort of song, why don't people do more of them?" (JJ)
/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Simulcra.sid:
TITLE: Simulcra [from the Amiga game]
 ARTIST: Jason Page
/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Sonic_Dreams.s:
COMMENT: "This was my entry for the 2004 SidWine competition, and it did
         fantasitcally badly, despite being what I consider to be probably the
         best demoscene style song that I've done on the C64. I actually spent
         a lot of time on this song, and I was quite proud of how it turned out
         when it was finished. It makes extensive use of the TFX wave table
         variables to try and squeeze two melody lines into a single channel,
         and the NoPulse command to control pulse width modulation reset more
         finely.
         The song is dedicated to a group I used to be a part of, Sonic Dreams,
         which is another story." (JJ)
/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Sunset_Spirals:
TITLE: Sunset Spirals [from the Impulse Tracker module]
 ARTIST: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)
COMMENT: "This is, musically, probably the best thing that I have ever done on
         the C64. Ironically, all of my C64 friends complained that it was off
         key, etc, and all of my PC friends love this version. Yet I had
         exactly the opposite reaction to the original version (c64 guys tended
         to like it, pc guys tended to complain that it was off key.). For the
         record, except for one or two notes, because I ran out of arpeggios (I
         do that a lot... there are two or three other musics which got
         scrapped half way through because I ran out of arpeggios. Thankfully,
         we've come up with a solution to this in the new version of TFX :)),
         the notes are NOT off key, and I don't care what you all think :-p.
         Said PC guys decided to take ownership of this song, and wanted me to
         create more like it, but I havn't had the motivation to actully
         finish any of them. (There are many, many, many stories that I could
         tell about the digiradi guys, but that's for another day, but the
         credit of the music to "Coder" is a part of that insanity. They were
         great times)." (JJ)

/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/TFX_Equals_Fut:
COMMENT: "Who could forget the 50 trillion intro tunes made in FC during the
         late 80's and early 90's? You know you love them... of course, I
         completly fucked it up by not using the traditional filterbass that
         everyone used/uses so that I could have a filterlead, but eh,
         do you really care that it's not genuine FC style?" (JJ)
COMMENT: "This is the second thing that I did for Digiradi, after sunset. It
         obviously didn't work as well as sunset did, but I think it has a
         certain charm to it, myself." (JJ)
TITLE: This is Coder

         another remix of this, with drums and related things, but I love the
         "pure" sound that this one has." (JJ)

/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Tim_Got_High.s:
COMMENT: "The Tim in question is Tim Bray, who does an act "Casionova", where
         he shows off 80's home keyboards, and other chip instruments,
         including a Commodore 64 with a guitar strap attached. Loscha and I
         were at one of his gigs, and he was tanking really badly (indeed, we
         could remember more of the words to his songs than he could!). This
         was mostly because, we think, he was completly off the planet. So, we
         came back to my place, after the gig, and I was showing off the new
         version of TFX, and we wrote the bass/chord/drum line (which is all
         one channel) to demonstrate some of the new features. The file needed
         a name, and so we just typed in "Tim got high", and the name stuck.
         This song also has a lot of ring modulation (Joxstrap/WOW said too
         much :-p), which I love as always." (JJ)
TITLE: Winter's Dream [from the Impulse Tracker module]
 ARTIST: Andrew Sega (Necros)
COMMENT: "Back when I was writing music on the PC for 16 hours a day, every
         day, this was the demo song included with one of the many "this is the
         last release really!" releases of impulse tracker. I'd actually
         wanted to make a C64 version of this for a long time, but it took me
         until now to really work out how to do it to my liking.
         Throwing that piece of junk away to concentrate on C64 music was the
         best descision I ever made. I never was very good at it, anyhow."
         (JJ)
/MUSICIANS/J/Julian_Jaymz/Yawlag_Xard_Hc:
COMMENT: "This is the only released music made in the modified version of JCH's
         player that I was hacking up during 1999 (I had all of my stuff
         stolen, including the only copy of the player sources etc). I
         originally wanted to create Galway style tune, but changed my mind
         half way and thought I'd make a Drax style music instead, and then put
         a JCH style lead on it. Read the title backwards, and it will all
         make sense. This was also the first music of mine that I know of to be
         used in someone else's production (of course *I* use my own music, but
         well, it's crap, so no-one else does), which was a graphic collection
         by someone in Sonic Dreams (Rat I think). Those guys were great fun,
         and some of them actully liked my music, which was a nice change, but
         goddamn the organisation of that group turned into a clusterfuck :-p,
         But it was all fun at the end of the day." (JJ)
